claim: An attacker with 10% of the hash power (q = 0.1) catches up from z = 5 blocks with probability P = 0.0009137.
assumptions: The whitepaper approximates the attacker's progress with a Poisson count. Here the race is counted exactly: while the honest chain finds z blocks, each block is the attacker's with probability q (negative binomial).
From k blocks the attacker catches up from z - k behind with probability (q/p)^(z-k), as in the whitepaper; k >= z counts as caught up.
The merchant waits exactly z blocks after the payment.
plan: Sample the attacker's block count during the honest chain's z blocks 20 million times and average the catch-up probability. The curve gives z = 0 to 5.
